prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1450; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by phone. The claimant was driving a vehicle that struck another car while turning left at an intersection. The policy driver is the claimant, and the policy is in force.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney. The account of the turn and the impact was clear and matched the first report.

Entry 3: Responding officer's report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. The other driver's statement agrees on the left turn and the point of impact.

Entry 4: Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front corner and driver side. Some details in the photos line up with the claimant's description, though the photos do not show the full sequence of events.

Entry 5: No independent witnesses to the collision have come forward. The only accounts so far are the claimant's, the other driver's, and the officer's observations at the scene.

Entry 6: Claimant reports neck and lower back pain following the impact and has begun treatment. The reported injury is consistent with a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Medical records received. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of strain. No prior injury to the same area appears in the records or in the claimant's history.

Entry 8: No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file. A neighbor mentioned seeing the car with damage some weeks before the reported date, but has not provided details or a statement in writing.

Entry 9: Reviewed the damage estimate against the photos. It is not yet clear whether all of the listed damage resulted from this impact or whether some of it was there before. Requested a repair inspection.

Entry 10: Claimant has repeated the same account of the collision in each conversation, including the timing, the direction of travel, and the sequence of the turn.

Entry 11: File remains open pending the repair inspection, the complete medical records, and a decision on the neighbor's information. Next review is scheduled once those items are in.
